subject: High p95 spikes impacting Cartile checkout — request for routing/quantization exception
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@cartile.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@cartile.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: High p95 spikes on checkout-gen-api — need immediate help

Irene —

We're seeing a sustained p95 jump on our checkout route starting ~09:00 PST. Baseline p95 was ~140ms; now it's sitting around 1.4s and we've had multiple customer complaints. Timelines and visible impact:
- 09:02: checkout API p95 1.2s (spike), increased error budget alerts
- 09:05: user sessions slowed, several timed retries from our front-end
- 09:10: transient increase in error rate but no full outage yet

Attached a short histogram and a snapshot of our observability for the last 30m. Can Redwood run an immediate mitigation? The primary business concern: we have an ad campaign this afternoon and can't have checkout failures.

Asks:
1) Immediate mitigation to reduce p95 for Cartile traffic (routing/priority/temporary model change)
2) Short customer-facing note we can send to execs

Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Platform — Cartile

Attachments: latency_hist_20261104.csv, ops_snapshot_20261104.png

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.j@cartile.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High p95 spikes on checkout-gen-api — need immediate help

I ran the initial traces and here's what I'm seeing:
- Symptoms: p95 increase concentrated on /v1/gen/checkout endpoint served by gen-api variant v3-q4.
- Root cause (prelim): increased concurrent batch sizes + uneven KV cache residency for Cartile's tenant leading to frequent KV eviction hits on the hotpath. This manifests as extra fetches + degraded kernel scheduling under current fusion kernel selection for long sequences.

Short-term mitigations we can apply immediately (low to moderate risk):
1) Protective routing: create a temporary routing lane that pins Cartile traffic to a less-congested pool and temporarily raises priority. Expected impact: immediate reduction in interleaving latency for hotpath requests. Risk: small capacity and fairness impacts for co-tenants for ~30–60m.
2) Canary quantization rollback: switch Cartile's model requests to the pre-quant (non-8bit) variant of the generator (v3) for the next 30 min. Expected impact: reduce CPU scheduling overhead and remove kernel quant artifacts. Risk: 8–12% cost increase while active; minimal quality delta for short sequences.
3) Prefix-KV warmup: pre-warm commonly-accessed keys for Cartile tenant (best-effort). Low risk, low immediate impact but helpful for follow-through.

Operational plan:
- With Product approval we can enact routing lane change in ~7–10 min.
- Quant rollback can be applied via model-variant routing in ~5 min with automated fallback after the window.
- We'll monitor p95 and error-rate continously and roll back changes if we see adverse effects.

I am attaching a short CSV of the latency histograms we pulled (latency_hist_20261104.csv) and a playbook draft for protective routing changes (protective_routing_playbook_draft.docx).

Recommend: Product approves the routing + quant rollback for an initial 30-min window; we send a concise customer-facing note acknowledging the issue and the actions. If Product prefers we can run routing-only first (less cost) and keep quant rollback as fallback.

Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Hi Alex —

Thanks for flagging this and for the artifacts. We’ve triaged on our side and propose the following immediate actions to reduce p95 while we complete a full RCA:

Immediate actions (we will proceed if you approve):
- Create a temporary protective routing lane to pin Cartile traffic to a lower-utilization pool and raise request priority for 30 minutes.
- Apply a canary quantization rollback for Cartile to use the pre-quant model variant for 30 minutes (cost increase but lower latency).
- Trigger prefix-KV warmup for commonly used keys.

Expected outcome: we expect p95 to fall back toward baseline within 10–15 minutes of the routing change and quant rollback. We'll monitor and notify you at 10/20/30 minute marks.

Risks: small short-term cost increase from quant rollback; slight capacity fairness impacts for other tenants while routing lane is active. We will keep the window as short as possible and automatically revert after 30 minutes unless we agree to extend.

Please reply with a single-line approval ("Approve routing + quant rollback for 30m") and we will execute and then send a short customer-facing update you can share with execs. If you prefer we do routing-only, respond with "Approve routing-only for 30m".

Call if easier: 15-min bridge available now.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Ops — Redwood Inference
